titre: What the licence grants, and for how long.
lede: The terms below are short because they are real. A thirty-day grant is written into the licence file, anyone can read the public licence, and anyone can verify a deliverable. We also commit that the answer may go against us and recommend that you keep what you have. Where a term lives in the source, this page gives its path.
description: A thirty-day grant written into the licence file, a public licence anyone can read, a deliverable anyone can verify, and the path to each term.

html: The Evaluation Grant is written into the licence file. It gives you thirty days from first use, on your organisation's own data, for its own internal evaluation, and you may share the output inside your organisation. In plain words, it forbids three things: relying on the output in production, redistributing the software, and publishing the output externally. The period is extended only in writing, and anything beyond evaluation needs a separate commercial licence.

verif.p: It is the first sixteen lines of the licence file on any clone.

cmd.n: the complete grant, as you will hold us to it

sections.h2: How the three levels of the licence work
html: The public licence is PolyForm Noncommercial. Under it, anyone may read, study, fork (copy the source) and use the tool for noncommercial purposes, with no time limit. An organisation that evaluates the tool gets the thirty days above. A client gets a negotiated commercial licence. The public licence itself states that it is not what a client buys.

This licence is not OSI‑approved (approved by the Open Source Initiative), and some organisations exclude such licences by policy. Such a policy holds back an organisation picking up the tool on its own. It does not hold back a negotiated engagement. Like all licences of its kind, it ships without warranty, with a 32‑day cure period, the time to put a violation right after written notice.

sections.h2: When the answer is to keep what you have
html: The engagement can end with a recommendation to keep what you have. The code that produces that recommendation is in the public source, and that outcome does not depend on our goodwill. With fewer than 20 observations, the tool makes no recommendation. The validation dossier states that it does not certify anything. It assembles what a reviewer needs, and the decision is the committee's. On the corpus we measured, 3 of the 5 fields are already handled at zero cost by regular expressions. That cheapest possible answer is in the headline. The recommendation itself prints, in figures, what would reverse it.

verif.p: The script runs in one second and prints the recommendation with the condition that would reverse it.

cmd.n: the conclusion, with what would reverse it

sections.h2: What you send and what you get back
html: You supply one CSV (an id, a text, one column per field) and, if you wish, a filled questionnaire. Each field in the questionnaire is optional. What stays empty keeps this repository's default, and the report notes it. A missing figure never becomes an invented one. Running the tool this way makes no network call, and your file never leaves your machine.

You get back a measured report beside your own CSV. It gives rates per field with confidence intervals, the range the true rate is likely to sit in, and it quotes no rate below 20 observations. Under an audit engagement you also get a signed report, signed with our private key. Anyone, including a reviewer who does not trust us, verifies it against the public key that ships in the repository. The verification proves origin and integrity, meaning the report is ours and unaltered. It proves nothing about whether the figures are correct. That burden stays on the measurement.

verif.p: The verifier is a public script with no dependencies, and the key is in the repository.

cmd.n: either authentic and unaltered, or refused

html: The remaining terms of a paid engagement (payment, confidentiality, audit rights, change of control, precedence, and the rights in the produced report) are settled in the engagement letter, written before signature, with no renegotiation after delivery. They are business terms, so this page names them without quoting them. The letter is the document your counsel receives.
One rule from the public licence already binds the evaluation period. The output of an evaluation run is internal to your organisation. External publication is excluded from the first day.
